objective: Determine why DS1522+ failed to complete boot after R1600 to V1500B replacement, and establish the preparation needed before another rework.
reason: The topology candidate has offline evidence, but there is no tested deployment/boot path and no observed V1500B execution. Additional CPU replacement expense is not yet justified.

completed.result: Exact match to the analyzed official DS1522+ early code
130 module data bytes changed; eight synthetic cases across Model11h/Model18h inputs and four SMU high-bit values passed; platform8 table results preserved.
Fits within original extent; decompression, FFS/FV structure checks passed
8 MiB aperture captured; both BIOS directories and compressed early code match official image; live configuration data retained separately
Actual register value0x2 has no valid security-reporting bit; no authenticated-boot decision can be inferred
Subsequent normal boots overwrite current-platform fields; cannot recover failed V1500B selection from current variable
Recovery networking is independent of finding an installed disk system; the studied recovery image lacks Atlantic, so expansion-port behavior alone cannot locate the failure
Built 8 MiB candidate from the live capture; preserved all current configuration and all bytes outside the compressed target region. Physical SPI image qualification remains open.

No exact missing basic CPU-init prerequisite or mandatory extra reset/clock change was identified. The precise logical0/1 dual-x1 candidate combination remains unverified; no explicit prohibition was found.
Official RS1221+ factory-intended firmware uses separate logical0/1 PCIe x1 engines. Registered table, original selector and shipped device tree corroborate applicability.

blocking_gaps_before_recommending_rework.needed: Establish actual SPI chip/layout and readable backup, preserve current board-specific fields, and establish a working image-write/restore method. Current mapped read is not verified as a complete physical SPI backup.

Observe a controlled R1600 boot of the finalized minimal candidate, or obtain equivalent platform-specific proof of the authenticated boot path. Vendor update signatures are already known to become invalid after editing.

The generic logical0/1 dual-x1 precedent is established by official RS1221+ firmware. Still validate the complete DS1522 layout, its requested device/function mapping and actual link training; donor clock/reset values cannot establish the DS1522 board wiring.

Before CPU rework, verify physical serial capture on the working R1600 and have a recoverable diagnostic boot path with known PCI/NIC/SATA output. Current serial settings alone do not test the external capture chain.

residual_uncertainty_after_r1600_prepara: The same-CPU split now has a factory firmware precedent. An R1600 test still cannot prove the full DS1522 candidate trained links or final mapping on V1500B, replacement-chip fuse state, or electrical/rework outcome.
first_v1500b_acceptance_milestone: A diskless V1500B boot reaches a working recovery environment and obtains an IP via an onboard DS1522+ port; verify actual PCI endpoints and then normal DSM boot.
hard_stop_evidence_if_observed: A documented, applicable electrical/package incompatibility that cannot be corrected by board configuration.
Boot authentication demonstrably rejects the required modified code and no compatible signed or otherwise supported deployment route exists.
A repeatable V1500B boot trace identifies a stage that the prepared configuration cannot pass.
limits_on_hard_stop_interpretation: None of these hard-stop conditions has been established. Missing logs, absent security sysfs files, a raw capability register without its valid bit, and static code differences are not proof of impossibility.
